sources.text:
Non-regular files (FIFO, directory, symlink) at paths omamori reads hang or silently mislead it

> **Corrected 2026-07-30.** The original analysis named five `audit.jsonl` call sites. Those were
> closed by #457; measurement afterwards showed the paths still affected were different ones,
> including two that hang `hook-check`. The original text is kept at the bottom.

## Problem

`open(O_RDONLY)` on a FIFO blocks until a writer appears, and `fs::read_to_string` follows symlinks.
Measured across seven commands × ten paths (4-second watchdog), against `52a58fa`:

| Non-regular file planted at | hangs |
|---|---|
| `.local/share/omamori/audit.jsonl.hwm` | `audit verify`, `exec`, `doctor`, `report`, **`hook-check`** |
| `.local/share/omamori/break-glass.json` | `doctor`, `status`, **`hook-check`** |
| `.config/omamori/config.toml` | `doctor`, `status` |
| `audit.jsonl`, `audit-secret`, `audit-secret.lock`, `heartbeat` | none — closed by #457 |

`hook-check` hanging is the serious case: it stops **before** printing its deny verdict, so the
outcome is decided by the host's hook-timeout policy rather than by omamori. A same-user `mkfifo` is
enough to make the enforcement path stop answering.

Where it no longer hangs, it misleads instead. With a FIFO at `audit.jsonl`: `audit verify` reports
`Operation not supported (os error 45)`, `audit show` exits 0 with no output — indistinguishable
from an empty log — and `omamori status` reports `[ok] Layer 3 (audit) enabled`.

## Cause

The file-type check lived on individual callers. #457 added one to `read_secret` and, in the same
change, added a new caller (`with_key_store_lock`) that initially lacked it. `read_hwm` used a bare
`fs::read_to_string`; `break_glass` and `config` each had their own `symlink_metadata`-then-read,
which covers symlinks and nothing else. **A check that lives on callers does not reach the next
caller.**

A `stat` before the `open` is also a race, not a control: these paths are re-read on every command,
so an attacker gets unlimited attempts to swap the path between the two syscalls.

## Fix

PR #476. One helper (`atomic_file::open_read_regular` / `read_to_string_capped`): `O_NOFOLLOW |
O_NONBLOCK` on the open, `fstat` on the resulting descriptor, `take()` bound applied there rather
than to a prior `len()`. Sixteen call sites moved onto it.

---

<details>
<summary>Original issue text (superseded)</summary>

Five of the six call sites of `secret::open_read_nofollow` open `audit.jsonl` with no protection
against that path being a FIFO: `verify::verify_chain`, `verify::show_entries`,
`verify::audit_summary`, `verify::count_unknown_tool_fail_opens_within`, `report::aggregate_report`.
A single `mkfifo ~/.local/share/omamori/audit.jsonl` therefore makes `omamori audit verify`,
`omamori audit show`, `omamori report`, and `omamori doctor` all hang with no output and no timeout.

</details>

sources.text:
fix: refuse non-regular files at the descriptor, in one shared helper (#468)

## Summary

Move the "is this actually a regular file" check off individual callers and onto the open itself, in
one shared helper. A FIFO, directory or symlink planted at a path omamori reads is now refused by
name instead of hanging the process, reading through to a link target, or being silently treated as
an empty file.

Closes #468.

The issue described this as five call sites on `audit.jsonl`. Those turned out to be the ones
already fixed in #457, and the paths that were still hanging were not among them.

## Verified

**Local** — 1564 tests pass (1316 lib + 176 cli + 39 hook_integration + 28 + 5), `cargo clippy
--all-targets` clean under `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `check-invariants.sh`
/ `check-boundary-matrix.sh` / `verify-claims.sh` all OK. A real 290,440-entry `audit.jsonl`
verifies `rc=0`.

`run_config_enable_success_appends_audit_event_end_to_end` failed once during development. It is the
known global-`HOME` flake recorded in the #457 plan, but this PR touches `config_cmd.rs`, so it was
re-run rather than assumed: five isolated runs and three full `--lib` runs, all green.

**The measurement this PR is built on.** Seven commands × ten paths, a non-regular file planted at
each, 4-second watchdog. Before:

| FIFO planted at | hangs |
|---|---|
| `audit.jsonl.hwm` | `audit verify`, `exec`, `doctor`, `report`, **`hook-check`** |
| `break-glass.json` | `doctor`, `status`, **`hook-check`** |
| `config.toml` | `doctor`, `status` |
| `audit.jsonl`, `audit-secret`, `audit-secret.lock`, `heartbeat` | none — closed by #457 |

After: seventy cells, zero hangs, for FIFO, directory and symlink shapes alike. `~/.claude/settings.json`,
`~/.omamori/hooks/claude-pretooluse.sh` and `~/.omamori/baseline.json` were added to the scan and are
also clean.

`hook-check` is the one that matters. It hung *before* printing its deny verdict, which hands the
decision to the host's hook-timeout policy rather than to omamori — a `mkfifo` a same-user process
can run is enough to make the enforcement path stop answering.

**Mutation** — four guards, reverted one at a time:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `O_NONBLOCK` removed from `open_read_regular` | `a_fifo_is_refused_rather_than_waited_on` — *"did not return within 5s — it blocked"* |
| `reject_non_regular` call removed | `every_non_regular_shape_is_refused_and_named` fails |
| unreadable hook script treated as nothing-to-do | `hooks_symlink_attack_triggers_regen` fails |
| `take(max + 1)` removed | **survives** — recorded in the test's docstring rather than papered over. The length check still rejects the file, because the bytes have already been read; `take` bounds *memory*, which no cheap test observes. |

## Same-class scan

**Layer 1 (repo-wide).** Two patterns.

*Reads that can block or follow a link.* Every `fs::read_to_string` / `File::open` in `src/` was
enumerated and each production one classified: 16 moved onto the helper (`read_hwm`, `break_glass`
×2, `config` ×4, `integrity` ×7, `shim` ×2), 3 are `create_new(true)` and cannot land on an existing
FIFO (`atomic_file` ×2, `write_hwm`'s temp), and 3 are deliberate non-regular opens (`/dev/urandom`
×2, the directory handle used for `fsync`). 0 remaining, confirmed by re-running the scan above.

*Callers for whom "cannot read" now means something different.* Making a read stricter converts
some previously-reachable paths into errors, and an `Err` arm written when the read could not fail
that way may be wrong. All 11 new error paths were read:

- `integrity.rs` ×7 — every arm returns `CheckStatus::Fail` or `Warn`. Loud, correct.
- `shim.rs` ×2 — **both returned `false`, meaning "nothing to do".** Fixed; see below.
- `config.rs` / `config_cmd.rs` — propagate as `AppError`.
- `break_glass.rs` ×2 — `false` / `None` means "no break-glass active", which is fail-closed.

**Layer 2.** `ensure_hooks_current`'s `Err(_) => return false` was safe only because the read
*followed* symlinks: the target's content failed the hash check and regeneration repaired the
attack. Refusing to read would have switched that repair off — the fix makes an unreadable hook
script fall into the same regeneration branch a tampered one does, with `NotFound` still returning
early so a guarded command never installs hooks behind the user.
`hooks_symlink_attack_triggers_regen` is what caught it; it went red on the first run of this change.

`ensure_settings_current`'s outcome is unchanged — `merge_claude_settings` already refused a
symlinked `settings.json` and `ensure_settings_symlink_returns_false` pins that — but the refusal
now happens before the merge, so the warning moved to the read site. Rewriting the file is not an
option there: the user's real settings live at the other end of the link.

## Open points

**1. The issue title is now wrong, and so is its analysis.**
"A FIFO at any audit file path hangs verify, show, report, and doctor indefinitely" named five
`audit.jsonl` call sites. Those were closed by #457; the three that were still hanging were
`audit.jsonl.hwm`, `break-glass.json` and `config.toml`, two of which hang `hook-check` — a command
the issue does not mention. Closing the issue with this PR silently retires an incorrect analysis.
The alternative is to correct the issue body first so the record shows what was actually wrong.
*Recommendation: correct the body, then close.* Cheap, and the wrong version is the one a future
reader would find.

**2. `SECURITY.md` no longer enumerates protected reads, and that is deliberate.**
The section carried a count ("9 total — 6 via `O_NOFOLLOW`, 3 via `lstat`/atomic-rename") which this
change invalidates and which would need re-deriving on every future read added. It now states the
invariant — one helper, every read — and the table is scoped to audit-file operations, whose
individual failure modes differ. *No CI check enforced the old count, which is part of why it was
able to be wrong.* Worth deciding whether the new invariant should get a check instead; not added
here.

**3. `describe_file_type` names FIFOs, directories, sockets and devices, and falls through to
"not a regular file" for anything else.**
On Unix the fallback is unreachable in practice. It exists so the function cannot panic or mislead
on a platform that grows a type, and so the non-Unix build compiles. Called out because an
unreachable arm is the kind of thing a later reader deletes.

## Recommendation

Merge. The change is small in surface — one helper plus 16 call sites moved onto it — and the
measurement is the acceptance test: the same scan that produced the "before" table produces seventy
clean cells after. The one behavioural risk it introduced was caught by an existing test and is
fixed and pinned.
